vocabulary.note: Fara ka diɲɛ na fɛ.
Bɔra don ka tɛmɛ 6 cɛ 12.
Aɲɛ ka jamana la.
Bɔra don ka tɛmɛ 6 cɛ 12.
Awa ni masayaŋ, si tɛ sariya.
‘At home’ tiɲɛ na.
Tɛmɛ 6 san cɛ 10 san.
TV wala jɛnɲɔgɔnya ka diɲɛ na.
Sabaabu ka jamana la.
Fara ka diɲɛ na: sleep, slept, slept.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I get up at seven in the morning.
dialogue.translation: Suba tɛmɛ 7 san ye tun.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Then I have breakfast and go to work.
dialogue.translation: Kɔfɛ, ay suba sigi baa furu ye.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I work at home in the evening.
dialogue.translation: Kɛɲɛfɛn ye wuli la furu ye.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I watch TV because I like it.
dialogue.translation: TV bɔ ye sababi o ye mɛn ye.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Then I sleep at ten.
dialogue.translation: Kɔfɛ, tɛmɛ 10 san ye jɔ.

scenario: Asking about opening hours
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

vocabulary.note: A b’a ye ka k’a ye fana a ye jamana la don fɔlɔw kɛra.
A b’a ye ka k’a sara, a kɔfɛ a ye jamana la.
A kɔfɛ a ye jamana la don sabaaba ye.
A b’a ye ka taa tilew ye.
A b’a ye ka tile minw ye.
A b’a ye ka a to a la aw ka tɛmɛ kanu.
A b’a ye ka a taara tilew la.
A b’a ye ka jamana la don fɔlɔw kɛra.
A b’a ye ka k’a fɔlɔw kɛra.
A b’a ye ka a taara jamana la.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Can you tell me the open time today?
dialogue.translation: I ka ne se furu sabaaba bi la?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: We open at nine, but we close at five.
dialogue.translation: An ka furu n’a kɛmɛ, nka an ka sara n’a sanankuya.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: And on Saturday, until what time are you open?
dialogue.translation: Nka n’a tile tauni, san jɛnɛw sabaaba ara furu?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: On Saturday, we close at one.
dialogue.translation: N’a tile tauni, an ka sara n’a jɛnɛ fɔlɔ.

scenario: Choosing a dish from a menu
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

vocabulary.note: A b’a araɲu fana kanu ka diɲɛra.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: What do you like to eat?
dialogue.translation: I ni ye saara ka diɲɛ?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I like fish or chicken with rice.
dialogue.translation: Mɛ be sira ka diɲɛ kɔnɔna tɛmɛ tɔgɔ la.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: The fish is very good here.
dialogue.translation: Sira bɛɛ min fɛɛnɛ yaami bɛ yɛrɛ fana.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Then I try some fish, please.
dialogue.translation: O sɔrɔ min bɛ sira ka taa, jɛnɛ.

key_phrases.translation: I ni ye saara ka diɲɛ?

scenario: At the bank for a simple transaction
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of English

vocabulary.note: Siga falanw bɛɛ ka taa la a ka sira man'a.
A ka taa ye ko ka sira man'a ('more money') an ka tɛmɛ tɛmɛna ('more quickly').
A na a man k'a dɛmɛ don kɔnɔni kɔfɛ.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: I need money now.
dialogue.translation: Sika n filila bi.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Here is your card. Go there with your ID.
dialogue.translation: Kuru ye a ka karaba. Kɔ kɔfɛ jɛn a ka tɛmɛ card.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Will you give me more cash?
dialogue.translation: A b'a fa ayi sika bɛɛ?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes, I will give you the money now. Go there.
dialogue.translation: Ee, ayi b'a fa ayi sika bi. Kɔ kɔfɛ.
